title: lifedraft input contract — Canada overlay (target shape, Track C / #602)
$comment: Composed with schema/input_schema.json by input_contract.compose_schema() -- see that function's docstring for the exact, total merge rule (no fallback/or chains: every overlay key either REPLACES or ADDS to the matching universal key, deterministically). This file supplies everything that is genuinely Canada-specific: the closed province/account-kind enums, CPP/OAS/RRSP/TFSA/FHSA/RESP/LIRA/LSIF vocabulary and sub-shapes, and the per-person registered-room pool. Per DP#16, this file's presence (and the countries/canada package) is what triggers Canada as the active jurisdiction.

province.description: Long form only — one spelling (#595 flagged 'qc' vs 'quebec' as a self-inconsistent example in the old schema). TaxDataProvider's postal-code aliasing is deleted, not documented (DP#9).

product.description: Issue #826 (DP#7/#10/#12): a branded-product flag that triggers a Canada program module encoding the product's well-known, identical-for-every-holder rules. 'fonds_ftq' resolves to countries/canada/fonds_ftq.py: a 7.3% 10-year-CAR expected return and locked-until-age-65 illiquidity (plus the LSIF credit in lsif_credit.py). null = a generic account with no product-module rules (today's behaviour). An explicit account.expected_return / account.locked_until OVERRIDES the product default (DP#13).

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: CRA My Account > RRSP and TFSA > contribution room. (Also on your latest Notice of Assessment for RRSP.)
x-uncertainty.question: What is this person's actual unused contribution room?

room.$comment: The x-uncertainty band on contribution_room (#671) is a deliberately coarse, jurisdiction-level DEFAULT shared by rrsp/tfsa/fhsa/resp -- it is the room question's shape, not any household's answer. A document that knows better states a tighter plausible_range in its provenance sidecar (#660), which OVERRIDES this default per DP#13 (a default is a fallback for absent input, never a coercion of input that was supplied).

resp.description: RESP contribution room is a lifetime entitlement of the BENEFICIARY (child), shared across every RESP account that names them, not a per-account figure.

person_room.description: Contribution room is a PERSON-level entitlement, not an account-level one (a person's RRSP room is one pool shared across every RRSP/spousal-RRSP they own or contribute to — putting it on the account, as the old schema's per-bucket totals implied, double-counts a person with two RRSPs at different institutions). This is why account.room does not exist in this schema (migration-plan.md, hard decision #2).

as_of.description: Date of the Service Canada estimate/statement this figure is from.

estimated_monthly_at_65.description: Issue #650: the projected monthly CPP the person's Service Canada Statement of Contributions estimates they will receive if they start AT AGE 65 — the engine's cpp_monthly_estimated convention (retirement_transition.cpp_from_estimate age-adjusts it for an earlier/later claim). This is the one number the user actually holds; without this field there was nowhere to put it and the engine had to fall back on a defaulted/maximum guess (DP#32).

as_of.description: The date the estimate was produced. A CPP estimate ages — three years on it is no longer the same number — so a pre-claim entitlement MUST be dated (#597).

claim_age.description: The MODELED age at which the person plans to begin CPP (60–70). Distinct from a benefit_claim's committed start_date: the person has not claimed yet, so this is a forward-looking plan the claiming-age optimizer (#291) can vary, not money already flowing. Maps to cpp_start_age.

as_of.description: The date the OAS eligibility/estimate was assessed (#597). OAS is residency-based and paid from the year-versioned table (not a statement number), so no estimated amount is carried — only the dating and the modeled claim age.

claim_age.description: The MODELED age at which the person plans to begin OAS (65–70; OAS cannot start before 65). Maps to oas_start_age, and the deferral bonus is DERIVED as (claim_age − 65) × 12 months so the claim age is stated exactly once (DP#32), never as a separate, possibly-inconsistent defer_months.

opened_date.description: Starts the 15-year participation window (#597) — the load-bearing date the old schema never had.

conversion_date.description: Issue #708: an elected early CRI/LIRA -> LIF/FRV conversion date (DP#1: a date, not an age). null/absent = no early election; the mandatory age-71 backstop (end of the year the owner turns 71) then applies, unchanged. When set, the LIRA converts at the earlier of this date's year and the age-71 backstop, down to the jurisdiction's earliest-permitted conversion age (Quebec: none, sourced -- Retraite Quebec; federal/Ontario: not sourced, an early election is rejected rather than guessed). The year component drives the conversion calendar year.

lira.description: Present only when kind is lira or lif. No birth_year field (#599) — age is looked up through owner.

purchase_province.description: Residency AT PURCHASE, which can differ from the owner's current residency — kept explicit rather than derived.

is_hbp_replacement.description: ITA s.211.8: replacement shares, not HBP funds used for the purchase.

quebec_carryforward.description: Opening QC credit carryforward amount (not a purchase amount).

holding_amount.description: Issue #649: the dollar value of the LSIF shares held INSIDE this account's wrapper — an LSIF nested in an RRSP (the Quebec 'REER FTQ'), where the wrapper (RRSP) supplies the deduction/deferral and the nested LSIF portion earns its own 30% credit. Set ONLY when the lsif block sits on a wrapper account (kind=rrsp/spousal_rrsp); the credit is computed on this amount. null/absent on a standalone kind=lsif account, whose LSIF value is its own balance.

lsif.description: Present when kind=lsif (a standalone Quebec Labour-Sponsored Investment Fund account) OR nested on a kind=rrsp/spousal_rrsp account (issue #649: an LSIF held inside an RRSP wrapper — the 'REER FTQ'). No embedded employment_income (#599) — looked up through owner's incomes[]. No retirement_year/pension_start_year — those are DERIVED per candidate scenario from the owner's chosen decisions.retirement_age and people[].benefits.employer_pension.start_date, not authored facts (DP#1/#598).

resp.description: Present only when kind=resp. owner is the primary subscriber; subscribers lists all (joint RESPs are common for couples). Grant PROGRAM RATES (CESG %, lifetime maxima) are never config — they are code tables (resp_rules.py) and do not appear anywhere in this schema (#593).

allOf.description: Registered/individual account kinds must have a single owner, never joint.

Issue #649: the lsif sub-object is REQUIRED on a standalone kind=lsif account and OPTIONAL on a kind=rrsp/spousal_rrsp account (an LSIF nested in an RRSP wrapper — the 'REER FTQ'); forbidden on every other kind.
contributors is optional even for spousal_rrsp (defaults to [owner] when omitted), but meaningless — and therefore forbidden — for every other kind.

qc_carryforward_opening.description: Optional, heloc only: an opening Quebec interest-deduction carryforward balance (TP-1 Schedule L) for a family already mid-carryforward when this document's as_of falls. null = none/not applicable.

disabled.description: The explicit flag for 'no OAS' (#592) — NEVER expressed as annual_max_override=0, which the old schema's or-fallthrough silently treated as 'not set, use the code table' instead of 'zero'.

annual_max_override.description: null = use the year-versioned CPP_OAS_BY_YEAR table. A loud warning is logged whenever this is non-null and shadows the table (#595G).

eap_tax_rate.description: Assumed marginal rate the EAP (Educational Assistance Payment) is taxed at in the beneficiary's hands.

eap_taxable_portion.description: Fraction of each EAP payment that is taxable income to the beneficiary (the rest is a tax-free return of contributions).

study_start_age.description: Age (applied uniformly to every RESP beneficiary -- the engine has no per-child study window, #598 follow-up) at which the study period, and EAP payouts, begin (issue #578).

study_duration_years.description: Length of the study window that pays out EAPs before the plan winds down (issue #578).

used_for_education.description: A FAMILY DECISION (DP#30), not a government rule: whether the RESP will actually be used for the beneficiary's education. When false, the plan collapses (grant repayment + AIP) at study_start_age instead of paying out EAPs (issue #578).

resp.description: Grant PROGRAM RATES (CESG %, lifetime maxima, CLB amounts) are never config — they stay as code tables in resp_rules.py (#593). These five fields are the genuinely study-specific RESP beliefs the engine reads (issue #578's winddown fields joined the original eap_tax_rate/eap_taxable_portion pair in epic #603 Track C Phase 2b).
